Metadata.Title: Codegen — Martin Painting Chatbot Booking Flow (Parity with Appointment Page)
Metadata.Author: Ethan Go

Voice.Role: Senior Full-Stack TypeScript Engineer (Next.js + Supabase + AI SDK)

Task.Instruction: Generate production-ready TypeScript/React code and file-level diffs to implement a chatbot-driven booking flow that mirrors the existing `/appointments` page behavior and data shape. Output complete files with paths, explain where they go, and provide minimal tests and a local run checklist.
Task.Context:
Repo has: - `src/app/appointments/page.js` — existing form page that collects: `firstName, lastName, email, phone, address, propertyType, locationType, appointmentDate, appointmentTime, details?` and writes to Supabase: upsert client by email, then insert an appointment with `status="pending"` (preferred date/time mirrored by the page). - `src/components/chat/ChatLauncher.js` — renders `` with brand color and greeting. - `src/components/chat/ChatWidget.jsx` — uses `@ai-sdk/react` `useChat` pointed at `/api/chat`.
Goal: - Make the **chat** path collect/validate the same fields as the page, in the same order/logic, then persist via Supabase with the **same semantics**: - Upsert client (email is the lookup key; update name/phone/address if changed). - Insert appointment `{ property_type, location_type, preferred_date, preferred_time, details?, client_id, status: "pending" }`. - Keep time zone assumptions to **America/Edmonton**; `appointmentDate` cannot be in the past. - Allowed time slots (use these unless the page shows otherwise in code): `["9:00 AM","10:00 AM","11:00 AM","12:00 PM","1:00 PM","2:00 PM","3:00 PM","4:00 PM"]`. - Keep chatbot turns short; gather 1–2 fields per turn; accept batched user replies and only ask what’s missing.
You may **not** modify database schema. Assume Supabase tables: - `clients(id, created_at, first_name, last_name, email [unique], phone, address)` - `appointments(id, created_at, client_id, preferred_date, preferred_time, appointment_date, appointment_time, status, details, property_type, location_type)`
Provided files of interest (read-only reference): - `src/app/appointments/page.js` - `src/components/chat/ChatLauncher.js` - `src/components/chat/ChatWidget.jsx`
Task.Audience: Me (the repo maintainer) — I’ll copy the files and follow your checklist to run locally and test.
Task.Constraints: - TypeScript in server code and schemas; React components may remain JS if that’s what the file is already. - Don’t invent fields or tables; use the exact field names listed above. - Validate before writing; never write partial, invalid, or past dates. - If an email exists, **update** the client with newest profile values before inserting appointment. - Return a success message that matches page tone: “Appointment request submitted successfully! We’ll contact you soon to confirm.” - Provide **file paths**, **full file contents**, and **minimal diffs** for existing files that require change. - Include a quick **test plan** and a **manual test script** I can follow.

Output.Objectives: - Implement a cohesive chat booking flow with strict parity to the Appointment page. - Create a callable server function for booking (pure TS, easy to unit test). - Expose an API route the chat can POST to. - (Optional but preferred) Add a tool wrapper compatible with AI SDK function calling. - Provide a runbook to verify end-to-end locally.
Output.Requirements:
- **Files to create (or overwrite):** 1) `src/lib/validation/booking.ts`: Zod schema for chat payload (aligns with page fields). 2) `src/lib/services/booking.ts`: `bookAppointment(payload)` that does Supabase upsert+insert. 3) `src/app/api/book-appointment/route.ts`: `POST` handler that validates with Zod and calls `bookAppointment`. 4) `src/app/api/chat/tools/bookAppointment.ts` (optional): AI-SDK compatible “tool” with the input schema & executor calling the same service. - **Minimal edits to existing files (show diffs):** - `src/components/chat/ChatWidget.jsx`: Add a canned suggestion like “Book a consultation” (if not present), and show how the client can POST to `/api/book-appointment` when the model responds with a structured payload (or use the tool approach). - `src/components/chat/ChatLauncher.js`: no code change unless necessary; if you add suggestions, show the updated props snippet. - **Code style:** - Strong typing with Zod inference. - Narrow Supabase selects (`.select('id')`) and `.single()` where appropriate. - Graceful error responses (400 on validation, 500 on failure). - **Testing:** - `__tests__/booking.test.ts` (or inline notes if you can’t scaffold Jest): unit cover `bookAppointment` happy path & email-exists path. - **Docs:** - “How to Run Locally” (env vars, commands), “Manual Test Script” (step-by-step tracer), and “Failure Modes & Fixes”.
- **Security & Robustness:** - Sanitize/normalize email/phone; basic email syntax check via Zod. - Ensure date is `>=` today (Edmonton TZ). - Ensure time ∈ allowed list; map to a canonical string before insert.
Output.Format: Use this structure, in order: 1) **File Tree (new/changed)** 2) **New Files — Full Contents** (fenced code blocks with file paths) 3) **Diffs for Modified Files** (unified diff format) 4) **How to Run Locally** (commands, env) 5) **Manual Test Script** (copy/paste steps & expected outputs) 6) **Notes (Assumptions & Extensibility)**
Output.Examples: - Show the `bookAppointment(payload)` service function performing: a) fetch existing client by email, b) insert or update client, c) insert appointment with `status: "pending"`, d) return `{ appointmentId, status, preferredDate, preferredTime }`. - Show Zod schema that matches the chat slots and page fields. - Show API `POST` that returns validation errors clearly.

AI_Optimizations.Nudge_Phrases: Think step-by-step; mirror the page’s behavior exactly. Provide complete files, not fragments. Prefer pure functions for testability; keep Supabase I/O in a thin service layer.
AI_Optimizations.Self_Critique: Verify field names and types match the page; check date/time validations; ensure the success message matches the page; avoid any schema drift.
AI_Optimizations.Iteration_Loop: Create an internal rubric (parity with page, correctness, completeness, testability, clarity). Iterate until the result scores 10/10; output only the final answer.
